A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ewe research work. All 12 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2 provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report original factuality and helpfulness experiments with 8B and 70B models. Section 5 reports original ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports revised benchmark and ablation results, additional retrieval sensitivity experiments, and an original human evaluation in Section 5.5.

M1.justification: Section 3 is unchanged, including retrieval and fact-checking feedback, FIFO memory updates, conditional regeneration, and KV-cache attention aggregation in Equation 1. Revised memory experiments do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongFact, Fava, AlpacaFact, and Biography, with C4 and Wikipedia as retrieval sources. The added human evaluation and datastore-size sweeps introduce no reported new domain or generation task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators: base Llama models, RA, Nest, DRAGIN, CoVe, and CoVe with retrieval. The new human study reuses RA; the reduced RA passage count changes its setting rather than its method identity.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes RA's reported retrieval budget from 20 to 10 passages. Memory studies replace independent unit-count sweeps and a stated fixed-token shape comparison with joint configurations and broader length sweeps. V2 also expands refresh-trigger settings and introduces retrieval-threshold, datastore-fraction, and stratified human sentence-evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: V2 substantially revises the memory-configuration analyses and adds precision/recall breakdowns. New Figures 5 and 7 test sensitivity to retrieval thresholds and datastore size, while Section 5.5 investigates whether VeriScore remains aligned with human judgments when used during inference.

E5.justification: V2 introduces chance-corrected human–VeriScore agreement estimation using Cohen's kappa in Section 5.5 and Table 4. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises many scores: 70B Ewe/RA LongFact F1 changes from 70.7/64.6 to 75.9/72.7, with the changed RA setting preventing a controlled cross-version gain interpretation. Feedback-form results, refresh curves, and datastore rankings also change. New results include sensitivity curves and human agreement of 0.61 for RA and 0.65 for Ewe.

T1.justification: The memory formulation and attention aggregation equation are unchanged. V2 adds no theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption; Cohen's kappa is introduced only as an empirical measure.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the advertised VeriScore improvement from 2–10 to 2–6 points, and the introduction adds a human-validation claim. The central contribution and claim of improved factuality without sacrificing helpfulness remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds cross-document reasoning explanations for longer memories and dataset-specific explanations for retrieval benefits, including hypothesized compensation by fact-checkers for smaller datastores. The earlier caution about frequent verification is replaced by a claim that shorter intervals always help, despite nonmonotonic Figure 6a. Section 5.5 additionally interprets human agreement as confirming factuality gains.

D1.justification: The specified RA top-k changes from 20 to 10, and Section 5.5 documents annotation categories, sampling buckets, and label exclusions. Conversely, the replacement Figure 3 no longer specifies the 128-token memory length disclosed in v1. Existing implementation references remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged after matching relocated pages. No cited work is added or removed, and the positioning relative to prior retrieval and memory methods remains the same.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact. Rewriting concentrates on the analysis discussion, with a new Human Evaluation subsection, updated headline wording, and a corrected author-name spelling.

P2.justification: The analytical displays are substantially reworked: two memory-count panels become one precision/recall/F1 plot, the memory-shape table is replaced by a length plot, and retrieval-threshold, datastore-size, and human-agreement displays are added. Refresh-trigger plots also receive revised axes and legends. Method diagrams and the main table structure remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens diagnostic evidence through precision/recall analyses, retrieval sensitivity tests, and an initial human check of the evaluator. These make the method's behavior easier to assess. The benefit is limited by unexplained accounting between 200 selected samples and 120 annotations, the fact that kappa agreement alone does not establish higher human-rated factuality, and the verification-frequency claim contradicting Figure 6a.
